newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, fwd premiums ease.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr, fwd premiums ease.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Tuesday at 35.770/775 per dollar on improved supply of the U.S currency and poor demand, dealers said.
The rupee opened the day at 35.80/81.
Dealers said the rupee traded at a high of 35.805 and low of 35.770, with most of the day's trade between 35.79 and 35.795.

"There was good supply at the opening level and the rupee rose to 35.785 before some demand came in," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Then the rupee dropped to 35.79-35.795 where it was stuck for much of the day."
Late afternoon dollar sales by a big term-lender then pushed the rupee up to its closing levels, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) did not buy dollars in the spot or forward markets on Tuesday.
"The State Bank of India was also inactive today,"a dealer said.
"It looks like yesterday's demand was a stray affair," he said. "We are back to waiting for the RBI or SBI to determine the market movement."
Dealers said forward premiums eased on sales of forward dollars but the dip was marginal.
"There was some selling in forwards today," said a dealer. "Premiums fell by 0.01-0.02 rupees."
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Tuesday at 3.57 percent against Monday's 3.63 percent, dealers said.
